open-question.question: Which format are log lines written in?
open-question.recommendation: One object per line keeps every field machine-readable — and grep still finds a line by its text.
open-question.alternative: Write each log entry as one JSON object on its own line. Every field stays machine-readable. A line is harder to read by eye.
Write each log entry as one human-readable line of text. A line reads at a glance with no tool. Every field must be parsed back out of free text.

open-question.question: Which level does a run log at when none is configured?
open-question.recommendation: Info records every state change a user would ask about without the noise of debug output.
open-question.alternative: Log at info level unless a level is configured. Every state change is on record. A long run writes a large log.
Log at warning level unless a level is configured. The log stays small. A normal run leaves no trace of what it did.

open-question.question: What triggers a log file's rotation: its size & age, or a "nightly" <cron> schedule?
open-question.recommendation: JSON lines grow fast under load, so size bounds a file where a schedule cannot.
open-question.alternative: Rotate a file once it passes 10 MB or turns a day old, whichever comes first. No file grows past its bound. Rotation times are irregular.
Rotate every file at midnight whatever its size. Each file holds exactly one day. A busy day can grow one file without bound.

open-question.question: Are logs shipped to a central collector?
open-question.alternative: Forward every log line to one central collector. Every host's logs are searchable in one place. A collector outage drops or delays log lines.
Keep every log on the host that wrote it. No network path is needed. A search spans every host by hand.
